intended_object: The character table of a finite group G over an algebraically closed field k in which |G| is invertible (classically k = ℂ). It is the square matrix whose (i, C) entry is χ_i(C), the value of the i-th irreducible character on the conjugacy class C. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
Row `i` is built from `irreducibleRepresentation k i`, a representation on `Fin n → k` that is irreducible in Mathlib's sense (`IsSimpleOrder (Subrepresentation ρ)`). Its character is `irreducibleCharacter k i`, the `i`-th element of a chosen bijection between `Fin (Nat.card (ConjClasses G))` and the set of irreducible characters. That bijection exists because the library proves there are exactly as many irreducible characters as conjugacy classes. The character is turned into a class function with `ClassFunction.ofCharacter` and then read off on conjugacy classes with `toConjClasses`, a `Quotient.lift`. So the (i, C) entry is χ_i(g) for any g in C, which is exactly the classical character table.

The rows depend on a non-canonical enumeration, as they do in the literature, where the table is only defined up to the order of its rows. The module documentation says this explicitly. The library also proves that every irreducible representation, on any finite-dimensional space, has its character in the set, so no row is missing. Rows are distinct by injectivity.

Generality: assuming k algebraically closed with |G| invertible is the natural setting in which the irreducible characters are in bijection with the conjugacy classes and the table is square. It is broader than the classical ℂ. The body actually uses these hypotheses, since they are what make the row count equal the number of conjugacy classes. Mathlib has no character table definition.
